Pretty good. Personally, I enjoyed the first Judgment's story way more, but this one isn't bad by any means.

I also really appreciate the fact that that one guy no longer spam calls you every 10 minutes to inform you that the streets are filled with thugs again, that's a nice change in my book.

A very unique online co-op story driven game from Hazelight. I haven't played anything like A Way Out before. The game heavily relies on co-operation of two players in order to advance throughout the entire story. Sure the game might feel outdated in terms of mechanics and AI but it was released back in 2018. Still, I believe it doesn't really have any competitors in its own league.

If you are the type of person that enjoys story driven games but also find the idea of playing this game with your friends, then best time to grab A Way Out is during a sale!

Note: You only need 1 copy of the game to be able to play with one of your friends. The person that owns the full game can give access to another person of the full game via an in-game invite. The other person only has to download the trial version.

Used to only play this game on and off with the kiddos at random times. It has improved so much. The lag caused caused by memory buffer overflow issues has been almost completely resolved (at least for me). The UI is cleaner, the music is more varied and quite charming. The new maps, and easier matchmaking make this a solid new favorite. The unlockable in game cosmetic items and ways to customize your round of golf make this game twice as fun as it used to be. I can easily see myself putting in many, many more hours here now :D

10/10 for me.

The Co-op Experience: Yelling at each other to wait before using debuff cards, but nobody listens, they just keep nuking with everything they've got.

The Map: Mostly used by my guys to draw giant genitals.

The Loot: Choosing relics is fun because you all need to pick different ones. If you click on the same relic, the game makes you play Rock-Paper-Scissors to settle it, which is nice.

The Strategy: Communication is key, especially in late-game content. Coordinating your build plans adds an incredibly complex new layer to the game.

The Core Game: Aside from co-op, Slay the Spire is Slay the Spire: the absolute best, here with great additions and improvements.
my only complaint is that it is too short. have more cases for the duck detective to solve please! he needs the money to afford that sweet sweet bread.

+ If you buy Definitive Edition, you'll get the original Ori and the Blind Forest for free

+ Graphic: Beautiful
+ Music: Beautiful
+ Story: Great and emotional. Even the prologue already makes me want to cry
+ Hard and challenging, but still fair
+ Backup feature. This feature will track your last 10 saves. If something goes wrong, you can easily roll back to a previous save file
+ Better optimization than the original one
+ New area to explore
+ New abilities
+ New difficulties

This (+) are used to be my (-) in the original Ori and the Blind Forest  
+ Fast travel/teleport. It makes easier to travel across the map.
+ Key/button remapping. The original game doesn't have this feature, 
Unfortunately this was not in-game feature and it requires editing game file. But at least now I can change the key/button.
+ Now we can replay a complete/clear game and also revisit all the area.

Most of the negative reviews are entirely correct about the size of the finished game. 

But for 5 euros it is worth it for a couple of days of fun with friends.

So I'm not going to give this a negative score because I do think this is a great game. But I'm too old for parry-based gameplay and the game basically relies on it. The enemies are overly aggressive and if you don't parry them, they basically stun lock you. Overall the core gameplay loop is fun, just not the combat. Especially bosses who give zero breathing room.

You loved Little Nightmares? The Witcher? Inside? Edith Finch? Please just go for it, you won't regret any second. Absolute Masterpiece!!! Personal rate: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

Raft is a great twist on the survival game. Instead of running around on land, gathering materials to build a base and defend it, your entire world is your raft, lose it and you're dead. You can't just run away from danger and start in a new area. I bought two copies so I could play with my teenager and that was some of the best gaming we've done together, very family friendly but she wouldn't go into the water for the first ten hours so I had to do all the harvesting with Bruce around. Little shy on content right now but solid core game play.

The Deed is one of those RPGMaker-but-it's-not games. That is, RPGMaker was used as the engine, but it's not a JRPG. Instead, The Deed is a reverse who-dunnit, where you are the murderer, and must choose how to do it and get away with the crime.

The Deed is short and meant to be replayed several times(it took me roughly an hour to 100% the game), and I found it a pleasant experience, and for a buck not even on sale this will be a nice little short adventure for most players.

Note: Holding down shift causes the dialogue to fast-forward until you need to make a choice, which is very useful on replays.
Game needs Trophy/Achievements pretty fun though would make a great title for the PS Vita or any other handheld device.
Patiently been waiting a decade for Darkness 3. Realistic in knowing it will never come but optimistic enough to keep waiting.
Cool little game but I'd recommend waiting for more and bigger quality and improvement updates before investing.

Best part of the trilogy and big step in the right direction!
Bigger and alive world with more tombs, puzzles are challenging (at least on "One with the jungle" difficulty) and exploration feels more organic, new crafting materials and skill system, also massively improved stealth mechanics from previus games  with beautiful graphics and fun story.
Some things could be better (combat, animations, side missions), but the overall experience is excellent.

The game is really good, however, it is littered with bugs. The bugs range from full crashes, to awkward UI interactions, huge delays on turns and daft graphical effects like jiggling characters and vanishing guns.
Optimisation also leaves a lot to be desired.

Hollow Knight, but robots instead of bugs. And that's not some sort of dismissal, that is genuine praise. The game is extremely polished, feels great to play, and has the excellent level and enemy design. This is basically gold standard Metroidvania. So when I say it's "like Hollow Knight", take that for the praiseworthy comparison it sounds. Lovers of Metroidvanias, this is your next game!

Easily one of the best combat games I’ve ever played. The weapon animations, boss fights, and finishers feel super satisfying, and the soundtrack goes crazy. There were multiple boss fights where I literally wished the fight would never end just because the music and combat flow felt so good. Solid lore, great pacing, and totally worth your money. Chinese devs are seriously carrying the action genre right now while Western studios fall behind.

Before you release a game, make sure it works.
In my case, the game interface, by the way, taken from an inexpensive asset, refuses to read mouse button presses, i.e. I can't even click on anything, only the “ESC” key works.

I apologize, but for now I have to issue a refund.

I put out a request to add the option to toggle off chromatic abberation and film grain because it gave me naseau, the developer responded and said that they will do it. Cannot give anything except a positive review.

I've just jumped out of my jet, switched to my bazooka, shot down an enemy jet, threw a handgrenade (don't ask me which key I've used to throw it - maybe that it will be implemented in the future), killed 5 players on the other side of the map with it, climbed back into my jet, landed it on the roof of a house, clipped through the roof into the so pweety decorated living room of the house, knifed another 5 players  and got 100% of the achievements for it. But then I didn't know how to end the map (other than ALT+F4) bec there's simply no option for it. 

But all in all... there's so much more love, dedication and experience from previous parts of the series in this game than BF2042 will ever have. 

P.S.: There's also no need at all to use norecoil / nospread macros in this game! So good! :D

Review after beating 3 bosses: Game is very challenging, but also fair at the same time, thanks to how responsive and fluid controls are. I bought it to help me pass time until the release of Elden Ring and so far it does the job very well.
